title: A line on the bill nobody explained: the manager answers the next day, and the other advisor finishes the answer
demonstrates: A question about a bill on the web chat: the assistant explains the charge in general, cannot see the bill, hands over. The chat turns Urgent and stays so overnight. Slot 22 answers the next morning in eight words. The customer's reply gets a draft he does not touch; slot 24 edits it and sends it nine minutes later, with the figure, and resolves.

customer.name: Sharon Whitfield
customer.note: a customer of the Charlotte Pike shop; a water pump replaced the day before

scenario.what_happens: 'Shop supplies $17.55. Nobody mentioned it. What is that?' The answer comes the next morning: 'its on every ticket. 5 percent of labor'. She says she would have liked to be told. Jasmine tells her, properly.

timeline.text: I picked up my car from your Nashville shop yesterday and there's a 'shop supplies' charge of $17.55 on the bill. Nobody mentioned it. What is that?

Hello. I'm the assistant for Brennan Auto Care. I can't see your bill from here. In general, shop supplies is a small charge on repairs billed by the hour; it covers things like cleaners, rags and hardware. For your own bill I'll pass the question to the Charlotte Pike shop. What's your name and the best number to reach you?
Thank you, Ms. Whitfield. Your question is with the team now, and somebody will get back to you as soon as possible.

timeline.text: Ms. Whitfield, this is Jasmine at Charlotte Pike. You're right, and I'm sorry it wasn't explained at pick-up. Shop supplies is 5% of the hourly labor on a repair, never more than $35.00. On yours it was $17.55, on the water pump labor. It should be shown to you on the estimate before any work starts. If anything else on the bill isn't clear, message me here.

facts: shop supplies is 5 % of hourly labour, at most 35.00 an order; on her bill 17.55
the hand-over waited from 11:21 to the next morning
slot 22 owns the chat; slot 24 wrote the reply that explained it

why: Eight words, no name, no apology, and factually right.
The draft was ready 40 seconds after her line; the owner of the chat left it; the other advisor used it.
The owner of a chat and the person who helped the customer are not always the same row in Stats.
